title: Ensure paths reported by a single callback are unique
description:
Fixes #55.

A single file change can trigger multiple filesystem events, which were each passed through as a separate path — duplicates carried no information since only paths are surfaced to R.

- Enables libfswatch event bubbling by default and deduplicates paths in `process_events()`, keeping the first occurrence
- Consolidates the path copy into a single allocation, replacing per-path `malloc`/`free`

`watcher()` docs updated to note that paths reported by a single callback are always unique.

title: Fix configure probe to link-test system libfswatch
description:
Fixes #48.

The system libfswatch detection only compiled a header test, so a partial install (headers present, library missing) was misdetected and the link of `watcher.so` failed with 'cannot find -lfswatch'.

The probe now compiles and links a call to `fsw_init_library()` with the real build flags, falling back to the bundled build on failure.

title: Simplify build system to avoid cmake
description:
Closes #44.

Replace the cmake-based bundled build with direct compilation of the `libfswatch` sources into the package shared object via explicit per-object Makevars rules. No cmake, no static archive, no install step, and no GNU make dependency.

- Hand-maintained `libfswatch_config.h` selects features from compiler platform macros (no install-time probing).
- configure keeps only system-libfswatch detection, the `-latomic probe` and the macOS `-framework CoreServices` flag; emits `@cppflags@ / libs@ / @fsw_objects@`.
- Static `Makevars.win/.ucrt`; `configure.win/.ucrt` removed (`Biarch` kept).
- Self-guard fsevents/inotify/fanotify monitors so one POSIX object list works across all POSIX OSes (wrong-OS monitors compile to empty objects).
- Neuter libfswatch's diagnostic logging so the compiled package writes nothing to stdout/stderr (keeps R CMD check 'compiled code' clean now that `libfswatch` is linked into `watcher.so` rather than a separate, deleted lib).
- All source patches live in an idempotent `tools/patch_libfswatch.sh`, called by `tools/update_libfswatch.sh`, which also regenerates the Makevars and the POSIX object list.

description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the watcher website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file

title: Directly target upstream libfswatch
description:
We patched `libfswatch` to allow it to compile under Windows MinGW toolchains + to compile cleanly without warnings. These patches were contributed to upstream and have now been accepted with the merge of https://github.com/emcrisostomo/fswatch/pull/340.

This means we no longer have to maintain our own patched branch of `libfswatch`, thus significantly easing the maintenance burden going forward.

This PR:
- Repackages bundled libfswatch to directly use the upstream version (5c443d2) - should not result in any difference post-compilation.
- Bundled version only deletes unneeded files and no longer makes any other modification.
- Updates configure/configure.win with explicit specification of cmake options.
- Allows build against a direct pull of upstream `libfswatch` with no modification needed to the source.

title: Fix for inotify_rm_watch: Invalid argument
description:
Fixes #4 .

According to the inotify(7) man page:

> When all file descriptors referring to an inotify instance have
          been closed (using [close(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/close.2.html)), the underlying object and its
          resources are freed for reuse by the kernel; all associated
          watches are automatically freed.

There is hence to need to call `inotify_rm_watch()` beforehand in the destructor. Removing this indeed fixes the spurious output. Fixed in bundled source package source here: https://github.com/shikokuchuo/fswatch/commit/a37be38dd4dbb7e6397ea4847bf2a80f00ed4747

Checked using Valgrind that there are no resource leaks introduced by this.

title: Fix eln2 function pointer type to match later's execLaterNative2
description: `later::execLaterNative2` has returned `uint64_t` since later v1.0.0 (August 2019), but watcher declared the pointer as returning void. Calling through a mismatched function pointer is UB and is flagged by Clang's `-fsanitize=function` in the clang-asan CI job.
